svg.text: K8b Chamber wash after the meal (10 min)
Ceiling nozzle bars wash the tub; the drive wall gets only a falling film and the puck squeegee, so no jet drums on the door.
program 10 min, then dry 8 min (usable after 2)
next meal can start 12 min after the last hand-over
falling film Γ ≈ 0.1 kg/(m·s), 6.6 L/min recirculated
A FRONT VIEW (looking at the drive wall)
ceiling nozzle bars (aim away from the drive wall)
B SIDE SECTION: WHERE THE WATER GOES
rear bar: grazing along the ceiling
The day’s liquor washes the tub before it is dumped; nothing is held between 25 and 55 °C.
1/6 Scrape: P1’s paddle pushes floor debris along the fall lane into the well.
2/6 Pre-rinse: the two ceiling nozzle bars wash rear wall, side walls, ceiling, floor and hob glass.
3/6 Wash: the drip bar runs a falling film down the drive wall; P1, then P2, squeegee it in overlapping lanes.
4/6 The pucks hang on their pegs above the well; two side jets in the left wall play over them.
5/6 Rinse with fresh 85 °C water through the nozzle bars and the drip bar.
6/6 Dry: exhaust through the condenser; P1 squeegees wall and floor. The tub is usable again after 2 minutes.
